title: Your app needs real-time updates (live dashboard or collaboration). How do you add them?
description: Choosing between polling, SSE, and WebSockets: connection topology, fan-out, reconnection semantics, and fallbacks for real-world networks.

data.text: **Question:** Your app needs real-time updates (a live dashboard or collaborative editing). How do you add them?

Pick the lightest transport that meets the freshness need: **polling** (simplest, seconds of staleness, fine for most dashboards), **Server-Sent Events** (one-directional server→client stream over HTTP — perfect for live feeds and notifications, auto-reconnects natively), or **WebSockets** (bidirectional, sub-second, needed for collaboration, chat, live cursors). Then solve the real problems, which are the same for all three: **connection management** (thousands of long-lived connections, heartbeat/liveness), **fan-out topology** (the app server can't hold every connection — use a pub/sub layer: Redis/NATS/Kafka feeding connection nodes), **reconnection with recovery** (missed messages during a disconnect must be replayed via a sequence id or refetch-on-reconnect), and **degradation** (corporate proxies kill WebSockets — fall back to SSE, then polling; show honest staleness states).

**Transport decision matrix:**
- Polling every N seconds: trivial ops, works everywhere, latency = N, load = requests × clients; smart polling (ETag/delta) reduces cost
- SSE: server→client only, plain HTTP (proxies/TLS friendly), built-in Last-Event-ID resume, browsers reconnect automatically; use for feeds, notifications, live metrics
- WebSockets: full duplex, lowest latency; needs sticky sessions or a shared pub/sub, heartbeat/ping-pong, and careful load-balancer config; required for collaborative editing (CRDT/OT ops flow both ways)

**Server-side architecture:**
- Connection layer: stateless **realtime nodes** hold sockets; each connection subscribes to topics (dashboard id, user id, room id)
- Fan-out: business services publish domain events to Redis pub/sub, NATS, or Kafka; realtime nodes consume and push to subscribed connections — app servers never talk to sockets directly
- Scale math: a node holds thousands of connections; scale horizontally; connection migration on deploy (drain: stop accepting, send reconnect signal, wait)
- Heartbeats every 30–60s detect dead connections (half-open TCP, sleeping phones); reap them promptly or connection tables rot

**Recovery semantics — the part everyone forgets:**
- A client disconnected for 40s missed events; options: (a) sequence numbers per topic and replay from last seen id; (b) refetch snapshot on reconnect and swap to live tail; (c) versioned state where the snapshot IS the source of truth
- Client side: exponential backoff reconnect, refetch-on-reconnect as baseline, visible 'live / reconnecting / delayed' indicator — honesty beats pretending

**Browser realities:**
- Mobile background tabs freeze timers and throttle sockets — design for suspend/resume (refetch on visibilitychange)
- Proxies (corporate, some carriers) drop or block WebSockets — detect connect failure and downgrade to SSE/polling
- Auth the connection at upgrade time (cookie/token in handshake), and authorize every topic subscription server-side

data.title: SSE feed with replay, and the WebSocket fallback chain
Reconnect is the normal case, not the exception
data.text: Phone tunnels, laptop sleep, deploys, and proxy timeouts mean clients WILL disconnect regularly. If your design only works on a perfectly stable socket, it doesn't work. Every real-time feature needs a defined recovery story — snapshot, replay, or version check — and a UI state that tells the truth about freshness.

items: Business services writing directly to sockets — fan-out must go through pub/sub or it doesn't scale
No heartbeat — dead half-open connections accumulate until the node OOMs
Forgetting replay: a reconnecting client silently misses events forever
Choosing WebSockets for a read-only dashboard — SSE or polling is simpler and proxy-proof
Authorizing the handshake but not topic subscriptions — IDOR across channels
Deploying realtime nodes without drain/rolling connection migration — every release is a global disconnect with no recovery
How do you handle thousands of connections on one node — and what's the real limit?
How does collaborative editing change the requirements (CRDT/OT)?
How do you test reconnection behavior deterministically?
How do you secure topic authorization at scale?

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Polling → SSE → WebSockets: pick by direction and latency need
Realtime nodes hold connections; pub/sub (Redis/NATS/Kafka) fans out events
Recovery is mandatory: snapshot baseline + sequence replay + honest UI states
Heartbeats, drain-on-deploy, and transport fallbacks keep it alive in the wild
data.takeaway: Real-time isn't the socket — it's the reconnect: design the recovery path first, and the transport choice becomes almost easy.
